4372b717ece66dec4580740d1e43b840fe943e36.summary: Flashpoint reports a new FIN7-linked attack panel called Astra, plus SQLRat and DNSbot malware, in campaigns it dates to May to July 2018, possibly back to January 2018. Lures were phishing emails with malicious documents. The samples use scheduled tasks for persistence and DNS-based command channels. The report cites DoJ indictments for the Combi Security front company and for FIN7 theft of more than 15 million payment card records from US businesses. The FIN7 link is the report's own linking, not a confirmed finding.

43841c4910e94161d703c45008c037fe5c043665.summary: Symantec white paper dated August 31, 2020 on threats to the financial sector. It reports malware and ransomware detections trending upwards from January 2019 to May 2020, the WastedLocker ransomware campaign, the Travelex ransomware attack, and background on APT and cyber-crime groups. The main focus is Jointworm, described as financially motivated and active since 2017, running a campaign since December 2019 against financial services and IT and fintech firms in Europe, the U.S. and elsewhere.

hedges: The report says Jointworm 'appears to be financially motivated'.
Lazarus's link to North Korea is the FBI's stated view, as cited by the report.
The loader is 'believed to originate' from Golden Chicken, per the report.
FIN7 and Carbanak 'are believed by some to be the same group', but Symantec still tracks them as two separate entities.
It was speculated that Carbanak could have made up to $1 billion in those attack campaigns.
Travelex said it never saw evidence that the attackers stole data; the 5 GB figure is only 'allegedly' reported.
Based on the file names used by Jointworm, it is likely the group is using OCX files to load Metasploit and Cobalt Strike modules.
The report cannot see what additional information Jointworm is exfiltrating in this campaign; past campaigns involved stolen financial data.
